option: (a) A country field and the store's address, set by the seller
needs: Nothing particular in any market.
note: A reading: the field holds Yemen whichever of its two areas the store is in (YK-12); what differs by area is S02-D3's and S02-D7's.

option: (b) A business entity holds it: a legal entity with its own address, assignable to markets
needs: A legal business behind the store, a person trading alone or a company, with its country and address; to trade from a shop, an entry in the commercial register.
as_of: YE-B102, YE-B104, YE-B105, YE-B106: 1991 (effective); YE-F416: 1991-04-13 (effective, as amended); YE-B253: 2026-10-10 (captured); YE-B268: 2024-01-08; YE-B156 to YE-B158: 2010
note: The 1991 law bars trading in a shop to anyone not entered in the register of the shop's district (read as two facts: one entered may trade in a shop; one not entered may not; trading with no shop, such as online only, is not addressed). An individual merchant applies within 60 days of starting to trade, a company within 60 days of starting its activity (1991); a page the records place in the Houthis' area gives 30 days from founding or licensing (captured 2026-10-10), and the Sana'a ministry's register is electronic only (2024-01-08). The Minister may exempt small merchants the regulation defines. A seller's documents to consumers, electronic ones included, must show its name, address, phones and commercial register number (2010 regulation of Law 46 of 2008). The records hold no register rule for the government's area beyond the 1991 law, and nothing on whether one area's registration counts in the other (S-07's).

option: (c) The billing address the merchant pays the platform from
needs: A way to pay the platform's fees from abroad, issued in the seller's country, so that the billing address is there: a card or wallet that pays foreign sites.
as_of: YE-D914, YE-D915, YE-D162: 2026-10-10 (issuers' pages, captured); YE-D103: 2025-06-15
note: Kuraimi's Pluto Debit Mastercard is offered for use 'inside Yemen or around the world', and MEPS's National Wallet card for paying on global shopping platforms (each issuer's own page). A 2025 article: paying foreign platforms in rials through some banks is limited to one or two wallets and not available in every governorate. Which provider Sharrwah bills through, and whether it takes these cards, is S-11's.

option: (e) The store's currency beside its address
needs: A store currency, read beside the address as the country's own.
note: The rial's one code covers two currency areas, old notes in the Houthis' north and new notes in the government's south and east (2026-10-10), at 533 rials to the dollar in Sana'a (old notes, 2026-10-08) and 1,562 buying in Aden (2026-10-10). Domestic sales must be paid in rials, yet the Saudi riyal dominates dealings in Aden and the government's areas, and some online stores price in dollars or only in Saudi riyals (S02-D7 (a)). A reading: a store's currency in Yemen may name neither its country nor its area.

option: Every option, (a) to (d)
needs: For the rules that differ by the seller's place to follow a move, the move must be a change of country.
evidence: YK-12 (YE-E1308, YE-E1289); YA-44 (YE-A005, YE-D423); YK-124 (YE-D521; corrections.md)
product_gap: A seller who moves between two such areas of one country changes the authorities and the currency area it answers to while its country stays the same. A move defined as a change of country doesn't catch it, so the checks a move runs (this decision's recommendation) would not run. Same root as S02-D3's gap.
note: A reading from these facts: a seller moving between Sana'a and Aden stays in Yemen but moves between two currency areas and between the two central banks' areas; payment providers from Sana'a are not authorised to operate in Aden without separate infrastructure in the South (2024-04-05; corrections.md: one direction only; read as two facts: without it they may not; that they may with it is not stated).

option: (a) The merchant's country (terms, the platform's payment service, other providers, fees, features)
needs: Every rule that follows the seller's place to be one per country.
evidence: YA-160 (YE-D012, YE-E785); YA-165 (YE-F352, YE-E795); YK-209 (YE-B102); YK-12 (YE-E1289, YE-E892, YE-D422, YE-D423, YE-E1308); YA-44 (YE-A005, YE-A088; YE-D435 and YE-D436 at place not stated, as corrections.md places them); YA-102 (YE-D113, YE-E193; corrections.md caution); YK-124 (YE-D520, YE-D521; corrections.md); YA-15 (YE-E1307, YE-C048); YA-03 (YE-B027, YE-E669); YA-25 (YE-D807, YE-E467, YE-E934); YA-26 (YE-D107); cases YC-116, YC-117, YC-119, YC-288, YC-101
product_gap: Where one country's areas answer to different authorities for payment services, the currency and the exchange rate, a rule keyed on the seller's country gives one answer for areas whose answers differ. The seller's area within the country, which the business record's address holds, may need to be a key beside the country. A reading of register.tsv: S02-E2 keys these rules on the country, and none of this decision's options keys on an area within one.
note: One per country in the records: the general sales tax, 5 percent of sales of goods and services; what a registered seller's invoice shows, the buyer's name, address and tax registration number among them; the 1991 commercial register law. Per area: two central banks, in Sana'a and Aden, whose decisions and policies on exchange companies conflict (2026-07-10); institutions operating nationwide answer to both (2024-04-05); the Sana'a bank licenses banking in its area (2024-05-31); the Aden bank issued rules for payment-service providers (2022-09-21), while on the Sana'a side non-banks were made eligible for e-rial services (corrections.md's caution: state the rule per area); the World Bank finds the two regions' payment frameworks similar, but Sana'a providers are not authorised in Aden without separate infrastructure in the South (2024-04-05; read as two facts, as S02-D2); each area has its own notes and central-bank rate (S02-D7). A reading: which providers a seller can use, and its starting currency, follow its area, not only its country. Changing (Q2's cases): each side barred the other's banks in May 2024 (YC-116, YC-117), and both agreed in July 2024 to cancel those decisions (partly reversed, 2026-02); Aden barred 12 wallets in June 2024 (YC-119, YC-288; 'licensed ones only', read as two facts: licensed wallets allowed, the 12 named barred), later reversed (2025-06-15); Aden provided in 2024 for withdrawing notes printed before 2016 (YC-101). No case varies YK-12 itself: one currency and one central bank for the whole country is a constant of the records.

note: The records name the currency areas by authority and direction ('the north', 'the south and east'), not by governorate, and hold no axis for who holds which place, so Q2 has no case of the bounds moving.

needs: Nothing particular in any market.

option: (a) A value per market
needs: Nothing particular in any market.
evidence: YK-124 (YE-D521; corrections.md); YK-452 (YE-E082, YE-E083, YE-F086, YE-F087; corrections.md); YA-139 (YE-D050); YA-177 (YE-D606)
note: Facts that differ by area, for settings this decision lists: payment methods (Sana'a providers not authorised in Aden without separate infrastructure in the South; a community-written client of Kuraimi's E-Pay sets which currency zone's customers it accepts, old, new or all, which corrections.md says is not the provider's documentation); shipping (difficult between some governorates; the Houthi authorities treated their areas as an independent state, so that buying goods from them became like importing); the currency (S02-D7). A reading: a value per market holds these only where a market can follow an area (S02-D4 (a), unknown).

needs: Nothing particular in any market.

needs: Nothing particular in any market.

option: (d) Narrower keys: checkout fields by the buyer's country (the address form)
needs: The fields of a delivery address in the buyer's country.
what_would_show_it: A source giving the fields a delivery address in Yemen uses (the postal operator's or a courier's address form, or a reference address dataset); Stage 1's records hold none.
note: What a registered seller's tax invoice shows of the buyer is held (name, address and tax registration number: YE-F352, 2002-05-25; YE-E795, 2022-01-01), under S02-D3 (a).

option: (a) A currency per market
needs: A currency for each market the store sells to in the country that its buyers there can pay in: the rial, in the notes of their currency area, or a foreign currency where the law allows it.
product_gap: One currency code can cover two currency areas of one country, with notes one area doesn't accept and exchange rates about three to one apart. A currency held by its code, a conversion rate held per currency pair, and an amount stored with its code can't tell the areas apart, and a rate quoted for the code may match neither area. A market's currency may need to name its currency area, or its rate be set per market. Whether a reference holds a rate per market rather than per currency is not in register.tsv's options; S02-VP-50's variants would show it.
note: Two currency areas under one code (2026-10-10): old notes in the Houthis' north, where the Sana'a bank banned the Aden bank's new notes in January 2020, and new notes in the government's south and east, where all notes were legal tender (2020-02-26) and Aden provided in 2024 for withdrawing notes printed before 2016 (YC-101: which notes an area accepts changes). 'Two currencies are in circulation, though only one is accepted across the country' (2024-04-05; read as two facts: one is accepted everywhere, the other is not). Domestic sales must be paid in rials (Council of Ministers' decision 13 of 2025; the government's enforcement, 2026-04-24; a seller may not require a foreign currency, 2010), yet the Saudi riyal dominates dealings in Aden and the government's areas (2025-10-28) and is widely used (2025-12-26), and some online stores price in foreign currencies (EB store: Saudi riyals only, read as two facts: Saudi riyals, and no other currency). A registered seller invoicing in a foreign currency must show the value in rials with the prevailing rate (Tax Authority, effective 2002-05-25), which names no currency area. Which currencies a market may carry is S-09's.

option: (b) Prices per market
needs: Nothing particular beyond (a): the seller sets them.
note: A price per currency area needs a market per area (S02-D4 (a), unknown).

option: (c) Prices converted by the platform at the exchange rate: one rate per currency pair
needs: An exchange rate between the market's currency and the store's that holds where the market's buyers pay, one per currency pair.
note: On 8 to 10 October 2026 a dollar bought 1,562 rials in Aden's market and 533 old-note rials in Sana'a, while an international provider's mid-market quote was 236.197 (Wise), matching neither; 'two separate monetary systems and two sharply divergent exchange rates' (2026-08-07). Changing (Q2's cases): 682 in Aden and 600 in Sana'a in January 2020 (YC-286); a record low of about 2,903 for the new rial in mid-July 2025 (YC-34); 3,000 before the Aden bank's 2025 measures (YC-305); Aden's fixed rate moved from 1,617 to 1,558 (YC-86); the government's area floated the rate before fixing it (YC-89, YC-306); the international quote's all-time high was 251, in September 2017 (YC-92).

option: (c) Prices converted by the platform at the exchange rate: a rate per currency area
needs: A published rate for each currency area.
note: Market rates: a local exchange-rate site for Aden (exrye.com), and ACAPS for Sana'a's old notes, 'Unofficial exchange rates sourced from YemenSul, Telegram'. Central-bank rates: the Sana'a bank keeps a ceiling selling price of 530.50 rials to the dollar in a daily statement on its website (2026-03-17); the Aden bank fixed 1,558 (2026-02-15; 2026-04-24), while the black market traded at 1,520 (2026-02-15). Both banks hold their rate fixed (2026-02; 2026-04-24).

option: (c) Prices converted by the platform at the exchange rate: the rates as a feed
needs: Those rates in a form a platform can read each day.
as_of: YE-B028: 2026-03-17; YE-E1306: 2026-10-10 (captured); unknowns.tsv's read: the capture of 2026-10-10
what_would_show_it: A source that gives each currency area's rate daily in a form a platform can read (an API or a dated bulletin), reachable from where Sharrwah runs, with its terms of use.
note: The Sana'a bank publishes its daily statement on its website, but Stage 1's capture could not read that bank's decisions and circulars pages from outside Yemen ('connection reset', unknowns.tsv, YA-88's read); ACAPS's own rates come from a Telegram channel.

option: (d) A price by the buyer's country
needs: The buyer's country: nothing particular in any market.
note: A price by currency area needs the buyer's area (S02-D4 (a), unknown).
